html:
The Kingdom of Mysore was a state on the plateau of southern Karnataka. On the 1783 and 1800 maps it is the realm of Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan, the strongest enemies the British faced in south India.

The Wadiyar family ruled Mysore from 1399, first as vassals of Vijayanagara. In 1761 their army commander, Hyder Ali, took real power. He and his son built a modern army with European style infantry and iron cased rockets, and conquered Malabar and much of the south.

Mysore fought four Anglo-Mysore wars against the East India Company, often with the Marathas and the Nizam on the British side. In the last, in 1799, the British stormed Tipu's island capital of Srirangapatna and killed him. They restored a five year old Wadiyar boy on a smaller throne; see the princely state of Mysore.
